defs.def: to hit a door, etc. firmly in order to attract attention 敲；击
to hit sth, often by accident, with a short, hard blow （常为无意地）碰，撞

ex.s: She was knocked down by a ball.
Though friendly, he could easily knock over my niece’s small boys and my six-month-old granddaughter.
ex.t: 虽然友好，但他很容易把我侄女的小男孩们和六个月大的孙子撞倒。

ex.s: I thought ___18___ myself, “Why would he carry all his books? ” Just then, some kids ran at him, ___19___ (knock) his books out of his arms.
ex.t: 我____想："他为什么要把所有书都拿着？"就在这时，几个孩子朝他跑去，____（撞）他怀里的书。

defs.def: to put sb/sth into a particular state by hitting them/it 把 … 撞击成（某种状态）
to hit sth so that it moves or breaks 打掉；敲动；打破
to make a hole in sth by hitting it hard 打，凿（洞）
if your heart knocks, it beats hard; if your knees knock, they shake, for example from fear （心）怦怦跳；（膝盖）打哆嗦

ex.s: Success knocks at your door only once.
ex.t: 成功只会敲你的门一次。

ex.s: It comes from the Cantonese word kau tau, which means “knock your head.” It refers to the act of kneeling and lowering one's head as a sign of respect to ___32___— such as emperors, elders and leaders.
ex.t: 中国人要求他们向乾隆皇帝磕头。

ex.s: Every moment Esmeralda discovered some fresh defect in Quasimodo, as her glance travelled from his knock knees to his hunched back, from his hunched back to his single eye.
ex.t: 爱斯梅拉达每时每刻都在卡西莫多身上发现新的缺陷，她的目光从他的内弯膝盖移到他的驼背，又从他的驼背移到他那只独眼。

defs.def: to make a regular sound of metal hitting metal, especially because there is sth wrong （尤指因故障）发碰撞声，嘭嘭作响
to criticize sb/sth, especially when it happens unfairly （不公平地）批评；贬责；挑剔；非难

ex.s: Eric Brown, only three years old, knocked Henry down when he fell.
ex.t: Eric Brown只有三岁，摔倒时把Henry撞倒了。

ex.s: I didn't think about it much until a morning last week when I knocked my favorite teapot off the table.
ex.t: 我没太在意直到上周一天早上我不小心把最心爱的茶壶碰到了桌上摔落。

defs.def: to travel and live in various places 漫游
（表示某物在一个地方但不知确切位置）

ex.s: Just last year, I was  56  a workshop when someone knocked at the classroom door.
ex.t: 就在去年，我正在____一个研讨会，这时有人敲教室门。

ex.s: Just last year, I was   56    a workshop when someone knocked at the classroom door.
ex.t: 就在去年，我正在____一个研讨会，这时有人敲教室门。

ex.s: Robutt would knock him out of trouble when he was too near a rock, jump on him to show how much he loved him, or go round in circles making noises as if he was scared when Jimmy hid behind a rock.
ex.t: 罗布特会在吉米靠岩石太近时把他撞开以免惹上麻烦，会跳到他身上来表示多么爱他，或者当吉米藏在岩石后面时围着他转圈发出声音，好像很害怕的样子。

ex.s: Adolph was knocked off, at a good sum, to the young gentlemen who had previously stated his intention of buying him; and the other servants of the St.
ex.t: 阿道夫以不错的价格被卖给了之前表示过购买意图的那位年轻绅士。

defs.def: to prevent sb from achieving sth or making progress, especially by rejecting them or sth that they suggest or ask 阻碍，妨碍（某人取得成果或进步，尤指以回绝方式）
to surprise or shock sb 使某人大吃一惊（或感到惊讶）
to complete sth quickly and without much effort 迅速而轻松地完成
to steal sth; to steal from a place 偷（东西）；抢劫（某处）

ex.s: Because we couldn't see where anything was, my friend and I knocked over glasses and dropped food.
ex.t: 因为看不见任何东西在哪里，我的朋友和我打翻了杯子，弄掉了食物。

defs.def: to make sb fall asleep or become unconscious 使入睡；使昏睡；使不省人事
to hit an opponent so that they cannot get up within a limited time and therefore lose the fight 拳击运动
to surprise and impress sb very much 使大吃一惊；使倾倒；给某人留下深刻印象
to make or complete sth quickly and often not very well 草草做成；匆匆拼凑成
to make two rooms or buildings into one by removing the wall between them 把两间屋（或两座建筑物）打通
to wake sb by knocking on their door 敲门唤醒某人

ex.s: I walked to the door and knocked.

Two hours later， back at my house，I heard a knock on the door． My husband（4）     it while I was on the phone in the dining room． "Does Jennifer live here？" I heard a lady say． In my husband's hand was my wallet， with not a penny（5）     ． She left before I could （6）      make it to the door to offer my thanks．
ex.t: 两小时后，回到我家，我听到一声敲门声。我丈夫（4）____去开的门，而____。

ex.s: Emily awoke to a gentle knock on her car window.
ex.t: Emily被轻轻的敲车窗声唤醒。

defs.def: to make a woman pregnant 使怀孕
the sound of sb hitting a door, window, etc. with their hand or with sth hard to attract attention 敲击声；敲门（或窗等）声
a sharp blow from sth hard 捶击；敲击；撞击
